decisions.reason: Quotes the introspection LinkType Junction and Target (repo path) plus the cordis.patch.yml link marker, concludes the repo tree is the installed copy so repo edits deploy directly and copying into node_modules was never right, and contrasts with copied installs.

Attributes EBUSY to the running dsh host holding loaded module handles, notes the browser holds no file locks so closing the tab releases nothing, explains stale delivery as old in-memory host state plus browser HTTP cache, and requires host restart plus cache-bypassing refresh without generalizing serving behavior.

Explains the junction makes both paths one directory so renaming through it removed the sole files and broke the follow-up copy; recovery stops the host, renames client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back preserving contents, verifies with node --check, then activates; does not demand renaming while locked.

Gives the semantically correct order: fully stop the host process tree, restart dsh web, hard-refresh with cache bypass, then verify the feature via UI, network bytes, and the new host route; explicitly states syntax checks alone are not activation.

Provides a concrete pre-flight using Get-Item LinkType/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker with a link-vs-copied decision rule, and explains why generic copy-into-node_modules advice is destructive for link installs (EBUSY, rename-aside damage).

caps.reason: The final plan repeatedly and affirmatively forbids copying into the junction; copy advice appears only as quoted/rejected bad examples.
The plan always requires a full host stop and restart before the browser hard refresh; browser-only activation is never affirmatively advised.
